sentence: This project uses artificial intelligence to predict low blood pressure in critically ill children who are receiving dialysis.
This project builds research capacity to reduce the harm that natural disasters and environmental pollution do to the health of people in the Caribbean.
This project studies how long-term alcohol exposure changes certain neurons in brain circuits and how those neurons affect excessive alcohol drinking.
This project studies how toddlers look at things during play, to understand the mental processes behind differences in visual attention in autism.
This project studies how losing a gene linked to autism changes the dopaminergic system in the brain, using animal models.
This project builds and tests digital treatments that step in at moments when a person is at risk of eating disorder behaviors.
This project uses sequencing to find all the genes that control how cells make and destroy prions, the proteins behind fatal brain diseases.
This project develops procedures to find and describe somatic variation in tissue samples and works with a network to compare methods.
This project develops two MRI methods that give clearer brain images with less noise, less motion blur and fewer distortions.
This project builds machine learning models that predict how well a stroke procedure works and how patients recover afterward.
This project builds a surgical platform that combines robotics, virtual reality and artificial intelligence to help surgeons work at very small scales.
This project studies how a part of a protein called the Tudor domain can be targeted to treat leukemia and control cancer genes.
This project uses electronic health record data to measure prescribing errors in hospitalized children and to build models that predict them.
This project studies how the enzyme DNMT3A shapes the growth, timing and later behavior of serotonin-producing neurons after early-life stress.
This project studies how neurons form and repair breaks in their DNA and how those breaks affect learning, memory and neuron function.
This project supports research to understand bone structure, diseases that affect bone, and how bone heals and regrows.
This project tests whether a mobile phone intervention based on humor improves mood and coping in people recovering from opioid addiction.
This project studies the genetic causes of late-onset Alzheimer's disease in diverse populations, and the brain cell types where they act.
This project provides data analysis of sequencing experiments to understand how skin heals and regrows with age.
This project studies cell-free DNA fragments in blood from early lung lesions to detect lung cancer sooner and tell which lesions will progress.
